title: Cold-Start and Skill-Aware Job Recommender Systems: A Scoping Review of Data, Models, and Evaluation Evidence
content: Job recommender systems support applicant–vacancy matching, but their reliability is uncertain when users or jobs are new, or information is sparse. This scoping review maps cold-start and skill-aware job recommendations, emphasizing early-career populations. Following PRISMA-ScR, we searched Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and EBSCO for studies published from 2010 to 2026. We screened 1,891 unique records, assessed 155 full texts, and included 76 primary studies. Fifty-eight studies specified at least one cold-start scenario, and 48 directly concerned early-career populations. Information representations, recommendation architectures, and evaluation designs were heterogeneous. Most importantly, none of the five field comparisons with reported real-world outcomes directly evaluated an early-career cohort. The available evidence therefore supports task- and dataset-specific performance claims more strongly than claims of employment benefit for first-time or early-career job seekers. We propose a six-stage evaluation framework connecting population definition, cold-start construction, information assessment, controlled offline comparison, human assessment, and prospective outcomes.
